description: Negative detector cases: near misses that MUST redact nothing. Each case's 'input' is materialized like the positive table (kind 'text' is a plain string; kind 'value' is a JSON value with optional $$bytes_b64 / $$latin1 byte-string markers). Every case asserts the value passes through unchanged with zero detector counts, zero affected fields, and zero affected records. 'protected' entries name paths that shield their value from masking by design.

cases.name: sk-token-one-below-threshold
cases.note: 15 trailing characters; sk- requires at least 16.

cases.name: ghp-token-one-below-threshold
cases.note: 19 trailing characters; ghp_ requires at least 20.

cases.name: github-pat-one-below-threshold
cases.note: 19 trailing characters; github_pat_ requires at least 20.

cases.name: slack-token-one-below-threshold
cases.note: 9 trailing characters; xox[baprs]- requires at least 10.

cases.name: aws-key-one-below-threshold
cases.note: 15 trailing characters; AKIA requires exactly 16.

cases.name: aws-key-one-above-exact-length
cases.note: 17 trailing characters leave no word boundary after the required 16.

cases.name: token-count-field
cases.note: Key spellings match whole field names only.

cases.name: api-key-id-field
cases.note: An identifier referring to a key is not a key spelling.

cases.name: mypassword-compound-key
cases.note: Case-insensitivity still requires the whole key to be exactly one spelling.

cases.name: passwordless-word
cases.note: Ordinary words containing 'password' as a substring of a larger word.

cases.name: secret-word-in-prose
cases.input: my secret is that I like trains
cases.note: A secret-key word in prose without an adjacent ':' or '=' is not an assignment.

cases.name: password-word-in-prose
cases.input: the password is hunter2 said no one

cases.name: uri-without-password
cases.note: No user:password userinfo means no connection secret.

cases.name: connection-string-empty-user-no-password
cases.note: Empty user with no password carries no credential; the password requires at least one character.

cases.name: public-key-block
cases.note: Public key blocks are not private-key material.

cases.name: private-key-words-without-begin-marker
cases.input: the docs mention a PRIVATE KEY without any block markers
cases.note: Prose without a BEGIN marker is not a PEM fragment.

cases.name: digest-authorization-structured
cases.note: Structured auth fields cover bearer/basic schemes only, per the version-one contract.

cases.name: short-bearer-word
cases.note: Standalone bearer values require at least 16 credential characters.

cases.name: empty-assignment-value
cases.note: An assignment with no value after the separator masks nothing.

cases.name: malformed-clean-json
cases.note: Malformed text without secret assignments passes through unchanged.

cases.name: protected-secret-key
cases.note: Protected paths copy their value through unchanged, detection included.

cases.name: protected-bytes-field
cases.note: Protected byte values keep their bytes; the binary marker applies only to unprotected values.

cases.name: reconciliation-identifiers
cases.note: Identity and sequence field names are not secret-key spellings.
